subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Ethical Persuasion vs Manipulation
description: One-minute skill: Ethical Persuasion vs Manipulation.

hook.text: Ethical Persuasion vs Manipulation: a simple choice shows how real behavior departs from strict rationality.

buildup.text: Thaler and Sunstein said nudges must be easy to resist and align with the nudged person's own interests.

discovery.text: Ethical persuasion is transparent: the person knows they're being influenced and the outcome benefits them.

twist.text: The line blurs with marketing. Companies claim to help customers choose better while designing choice environments.

climax.text: Ask two questions: can I easily opt out, and does this serve my goals or theirs?

punchline.text: A good nudge helps. A dark nudge deceives.

quiz.question: What distinguishes an ethical nudge from manipulation?
options: Ethical nudges are always free of cost
Ethical nudges are transparent, easy to resist, and serve the person's interests
